title: Tenant affinity hash compression collision routes production traffic to wrong region
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Production customer reported a surge window where a portion of their requests were routed to the EU region instead of their pinned US-dedicated pool. Root cause appears to be an affinity-key compression change that introduced hash collisions for high-throughput tenants. Collision made the routing comparator prefer a geo-neighbor region variant for a subset of requests, bypassing the tenant's dedicated capacity and causing errors and increased latency.
observed_behavior: Between 2026-03-11T22:14Z and 2026-03-11T22:48Z, 1.7% of Customer A's requests hit EU-hosted variants. Errors spiked (502/timeout) and latency P95 increased from 80ms to 420ms for those requests. Alerting channels showed Dedicated pool saturation but routing chose region-fallback instead of queued back to dedicated or throttled.
expected_behavior: Routing should preserve tenant-scoped affinity and respect explicit dedicated pool pinning. In capacity-saturated windows, failover should demote to compatible variant within same tier/region or apply configured fallback policy, not choose an incompatible region that lacks dedicated capacity.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy the routing change that enabled affinity-key compression (commit 8f3b1a2)
Simulate 10k rps tenant traffic with repeating affinity hints to force hash collision probability
Observe route decisions in policy-evaluator logs (debug routing.trace=true) and compare chosen region/model for colliding keys
Verify that compressed-keys with identical 64-bit hash sometimes resolve to the same routing bucket across unrelated tenants
impact: High — customer-visible errors and latency regressions for a production tenant with dedicated capacity. Potential revenue and SLA exposure. Affected both Hosted and Dedicated paths when the compression codepath is enabled.
root_cause: A change introduced to reduce affinity-key storage (affinity-key compression) replaced full tenant+hint strings with a 64-bit truncated hash. Under high-throughput repetitive hints, hash collisions occurred and the policy-merge code used the compressed key as the primary lookup for affinity, causing cross-tenant bucket pollution and incorrect region selection in the presence of tie-breakers.
immediate_mitigation: Revert the affinity-key compression rollout at service edge (hotfix revert of commit 8f3b1a2)
Scoped config: disable compression for tenants with dedicated pools via runtime flag routing.compress_affinity=false
Emergency scaling: temporarily increase dedicated pool autoscaling threshold for affected tenant to reduce visible errors
permanent_fix_plan: Rollback compression until a collision-resistant encoding is implemented (e.g., 128-bit hash or HMAC with tenant salt)
Update policy-evaluator to never use compressed key as sole affinity discriminator; fall back to explicit tenant-id when present
Add deterministic tests and fuzzing in CI to exercise high-throughput repeated hints and measure collision rates
Add telemetry: collision_count metric, per-tenant collision alerts, and synthetic-checks during canary rollouts
rollout_plan: Merge hotfix that disables compression globally (hotfix/revert-affinity-compress) — roll out to staging then canary 10% hosts — monitor collision_count and routing correctness
After validation, roll to production in waves by region with pre- and post-deployment QA
Once new encoding is implemented and tested, enable for non-dedicated tenants behind a feature flag and increase coverage incrementally
qa_steps: Unit tests for policy-evaluator to ensure tenant-id supersedes compressed key
Load test with 50k RPS synthetic tenant using repeating hints to confirm collision rate is ~0
End-to-end test: create a scoped dedicated pool and verify routing never selects other regions during saturation
Integration test: validate collision_count increments only when intentional hash collisions are fed
comments: 2026-03-12 — Aisha Kapoor: Initial triage. Suspect compression collision. Customer A oncall reported sustained errors. Escalating to SRE + routing owners.
2026-03-12 — Liam Chen: Rolled hotfix to disable compression in canary; telemetry shows collision_count dropping to 0 for canary hosts.
2026-03-13 — Priya Desai (SRE): Dedicated pool autoscaler bumped for Customer A as temporary relief. Recommended revert for full fleet tomorrow.
2026-03-14 — Design review: routing UX should display affinity compression flag in tenant settings; product to prioritize in next cycle.
